transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Yeah, it's nice to meet you too. Um, well, I guess I came in because... well, I just can't seem to shake this incredibly heavy feeling, you know? It really started settling in after we bought our house. I just keep feeling like I’ve completely let my family down by taking on this mortgage. It's a huge financial commitment, obviously, and I just look at the paperwork and think, what on earth was I thinking? 

I mean, I'm just a waiter. I took some classes in college years ago but I never finished my degree, and now I'm trying to support this massive loan on a server's wages. And the guilt about it is just... it's bleeding into absolutely everything I do. Like, every single small mistake I make at work lately—if I forget to bring a table their extra side of ranch dressing, or if I accidentally punch the wrong appetizer into the computer system—it just hits me so incredibly hard. It doesn't just feel like a simple error; it feels like it proves that I’m just totally useless. I'll just stand there in the back by the kitchen thinking that I deserve whatever bad things happen to me, because if I can't even get a basic lunch order right, how am I supposed to provide for my family and keep a roof over their heads? I just keep spiraling into this intense guilt over every little thing, and I can't seem to turn it off.
Have you ever felt this way for a period of time in the past, or is this the very first time you have experienced these feelings?

Well, um, to be completely honest, it's not the very first time, no. But this particular stretch... it's been going on for a really long time. I mean, if I sit down and actually trace it back, I'd say these heavy, depressed, just overwhelming periods of guilt have been hanging over me for about a year and two months now. 

And I remember exactly when it started getting this bad, because it was right around the time we were finalizing the initial paperwork for the house, which was just over a year ago. It was supposed to be this exciting time, you know? My wife was looking at paint colors, and we were talking about where to put the furniture, but all I could feel was this crushing weight settling into my chest. And it just hasn't lifted since then. It's like, for the last fourteen months, I wake up and the very first thought in my head is about how I'm failing. And it just colors the whole day. Even on days when the restaurant isn't busy and things should be easy, I just carry this... this dark cloud of guilt around with me. So yeah, it's been about a year and two months of feeling exactly like this, just constantly.

During these past fourteen months, have there been any periods of at least two weeks where your symptoms became significantly more intense, or where you experienced other changes like a complete loss of interest in all your usual activities, severe sleep problems, or thoughts that life isn't worth living?

Well, um, as far as sleep goes, yeah, I do have trouble. I mean, I'll be lying there in bed, staring at the ceiling fan—it has this little wobble to it, you know, just this rhythmic clicking sound that drives me crazy when the house is quiet—and I'll just be awake for hours before my early shift. The alarm is set for 5:30 AM, and I'll look at the clock at 2:00, then 3:15, and my mind is just racing through every single thing I've messed up. The mortgage, the tips I didn't make, the look on my wife's face when I told her I couldn't pick up an extra shift... it just plays on a loop. 

And, you know, you asked about thoughts of life not being worth living... I want to be clear, I don't have a plan to hurt myself. I really don't. I wouldn't do that to my family, especially with the debt we're in now. But... when I'm lying there, awake in the dark, listening to that ceiling fan, and I know I have to get up in a few hours and put on my apron and smile at customers while feeling like this absolute fraud... I do sometimes think it would just be so much easier if I just didn't wake up. Like, if I could just drift off and not have to face another day of failing at absolutely everything. It wouldn't be me giving up, exactly, it would just be... a relief. A break from the constant pressure and the guilt that I just can't seem to get out from under. So, yeah, those thoughts definitely creep in during those long nights, even though I'd never actually do anything to make it happen. It's just this heavy, exhausting wish for it all to stop.
In the past fourteen months, have you had any periods of at least two months where your mood felt completely normal and you didn't experience these heavy feelings of guilt or sadness at all?

Well, um... no, not really. I mean, if I really sit and think about it, trying to find a solid block of time where I felt totally normal... I just can't. There definitely hasn't been a two-month stretch where I felt okay, that's for sure. 

I mean, sure, there might be a day here or there where the sun is shining, or maybe we have a really good dinner rush at the restaurant and I walk out with decent tips, and for a few hours, the weight doesn't feel quite as crushing. Maybe I'll even laugh at a joke one of the line cooks makes, you know? But it never lasts. It's like... it's like trying to hold a beach ball underwater. You can do it for a minute, but it always pops back up. 

For most of this whole fourteen-month period, even when some days were a little lighter or I was distracted by something, I’ve just been weighed down by that empty, guilty feeling more often than not. It's just always there in the background, like static on a radio that you can't quite tune out. Even if I'm not actively spiraling about the mortgage in that exact second, the heaviness is still sitting right there on my chest. So, no, there hasn't been any real break from it. It's just been this constant, draining presence, day in and day out, for the vast majority of the time since we started all that paperwork.
